featured_techniques.technique: Inspect sway bar bushings for wear and slack
Inspect sway bar link and ball-and-socket for wear
Replacement guidance: consider replacing both bushings and the link together

sections.description: Len introduces the general topic and uses a 2010 Nissan Altima as the example. He highlights the sway bar and its bushings, explaining that stretched rubber can allow the bar to move and create noise, especially under load while driving over irregularities.
sections.title: Sway Bar Components and Noise Mechanism

sections.description: The video shifts to the sway bar link, pointing out the ball-and-socket joint inside the link. When worn, it can produce a knocking or banging sound over bumps, which is a common diagnostic clue for a failing link.
sections.title: Sway Bar Link Wear and Ball-and-Socket

sections.description: Len notes that replacing the sway bar bushings and the sway bar link is typical, and suggests replacing both at the same time. He also mentions 1A Auto as a resource for parts.
sections.title: Replacement Recommendation

summary: Len from 1A Auto uses a 2010 Nissan Altima as the reference example to explain a rear-end clunking noise heard over bumps. The video identifies two primary suspects in the suspension linkage: the sway bar bushing (rubber supports for the stabilizer bar) and the sway bar link (with a ball-and-socket joint). He explains that stretched or worn bushings allow the bar to move and create noise, and that a worn ball-and-socket in the link can produce a knocking sound when the vehicle encounters bumps. The guidance concludes with a practical replacement recommendation: if diagnosing these parts, replacement of both the sway bar bushings and the sway bar link is commonly done together, and the video suggests 1A Auto as a source for parts.
title: Rear Clunking Noise Diagnosis: Sway Bar Bushings and Link Wear (2010 Nissan Altima)
